⚠️ Problem: Learner spells 'rain' as 'rayn' or 'day' as 'dai'.
💡 Solution: Reinforce position rule: AI inside, AY at the end.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Basic Vowel Teams (EE, EA, AI, AY, OA, OW, OO)
1. Definition: A vowel team is two vowels working together to make one long vowel or diphthong sound.
2. Rule: EE/EA = /iː/ (see, eat); AI = /eɪ/ (mid-word: rain); AY = /eɪ/ (end-word: day); OA = /oʊ/ (boat); OW = /oʊ/ or /aʊ/ (show/now); OO = /uː/ or /ʊ/ (moon/book).
3. Why? English orthography uses vowel combinations to represent long monopthongs and diphthongs.
4. How to recognize? Two adjacent vowel letters.
5. Common examples: see /siː/, eat /iːt/, rain /reɪn/, day /deɪ/, boat /boʊt/, show /ʃoʊ/, book /bʊk/, moon /muːn/
6. Counter-examples: Vowels in separate syllables (re-act).
7. Exceptions: EA = /ɛ/ in head, bread, heavy, dead.
8. Common mistakes: Pronouncing AI at the end of a word or AY in the middle.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: « When two vowels go walking, the first one does the talking! »
10. Key vocabulary: vowel team, diphthong, position rule, long vowel, digraph
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟢 A1
13. Associated Visual: 🚶‍♂️ Two vowels walking together, first one speaking.
14. Key Takeaway: AI inside words, AY at the end! EE/EA = long /iː/.

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Which vowel team is used at the end of a word for /eI/: AI or AY? (AY, like in 'day')
CCQ 2: How is OO pronounced in 'book' vs 'moon'? (/ʊ/ short in book, /uː/ long in moon)
CCQ 3: How is EA pronounced in 'head'? (/ɛ/ short e, exception to 'eat')

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.
